status_summary: No FAA or DOT rulemaking to reform slot allocation was found; the Federal Register search for slot actions since 2025-01-20 returned orders and notices only. The FAA issued interim and then targeted scheduling-limit orders at Newark in 2025 (published 2025-05-23 and 2025-06-10), a scheduling-limit order at Chicago O'Hare published 2026-04-20 effective 2026-05-17 to 2026-10-24, and on 2026-06-23 published an extension of the LaGuardia order to 2028-10-28 with no changes. These are capacity and extension orders, not a slot allocation rulemaking.

timeline.event: FAA published an order setting temporary hourly scheduling caps at Newark through 2025-12-31, built on voluntary schedule reductions and not a new allocation system.

FAA published a temporary daily scheduling cap order for Chicago O'Hare effective 2026-05-17 to 2026-10-24, allocated by share of Summer 2025 schedules and citing capacity, safety and preserving the competitive status quo.
FAA published an extension of the LaGuardia slot order to 2028-10-28 stating no changes to its allocation provisions.

title: Rulemaking to allocate airport slot pairs on safety, capacity and competition
uncertainties: Searches performed: Federal Register API term searches for FAA slot documents since 2025-01-20 (31 results; the first page and part of the second were reviewed) and reading of the Newark, O'Hare and LaGuardia orders; no web search. Slot usage waivers, extension orders and the 2026-10-08 LaGuardia exemption for a single slot transfer are not an allocation rulemaking. The JFK order text was not read and the Unified Agenda was not checked, so a planned slot rulemaking could be listed there; the 2026-10-08 FAA exemption says the agency will consider certain slot concerns in future rulemaking, without dates.
